title: Tranquillity sent down
hook: He sent down tranquillity into the hearts of the believers (48:4)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was fath mubin: Hudaybiyyah, the treaty that felt like losing and turned out to be a door. Your line was an opening.

Back at Hudaybiyyah, picture the camp the night the treaty was signed. Fourteen hundred people who had walked for days to reach the Ka'bah, told to turn around. Some angry, some confused, a few close to refusing. The Prophet ﷺ told them to sacrifice their animals and shave their heads right there, and at first, the reports say, nobody moved. Anyone who has stood in a room full of disappointed people knows that silence. The surah describes what came down into it.

Verse four of Surah Al-Fath, in Pickthall's translation: "He it is Who sent down peace of reassurance into the hearts of the believers that they might add faith unto their faith." Peace of reassurance is Pickthall's way of rendering one Arabic word: sakinah. Its root, s-k-n, means to be still, to settle, to come to rest. The same root gives maskan, a dwelling, and sakan, the night or a spouse, in whom one finds rest. Sakinah is stillness you can live inside. Notice the verb: sent down, like rain. The verse doesn't say the believers calmed themselves. Calm was given into hearts that were agitated. And it adds faith to faith, as if faith can grow, layer on layer. The word shows up at other hard moments too. In Surah At-Tawbah, it comes down on the Prophet in the cave during the migration, when only Abu Bakr was with him and the trackers were at the entrance. A hadith in Sahih Muslim says that when people gather in a house of Allah to recite and study the Qur'an together, sakinah descends on them and mercy covers them. Scholars of language note that Hebrew has a related word, shekhinah, which in Jewish tradition names the divine presence dwelling among people: a shared root between neighbors. This week: kneeling with every nation, prayer at forty, the jinn listening, feet made firm, an unlocked heart, an opening, and now the stillness that comes down.
screen: `SAKINAH: STILLNESS YOU CAN LIVE IN.` · `SENT DOWN, LIKE RAIN.` · `IN THE CAVE, AND IN THE CIRCLE.` · `FAITH ADDED TO FAITH.`

segments.voice: Let your shoulders drop, and breathe in for a count of four, out for a count of six, again and again. Don't try to manufacture calm, since the verse says it is sent; just make room for it, the way you'd open a window and wait for the air. If thoughts rush in, go back to the count, and if you pray, you can ask for sakinah.
Sakinah. Stillness sent down into agitated hearts, from the root for settling and dwelling, in 48:4. Today's word.
Your line: tranquillity comes down. The calm is given; the room for it is yours to make. That's the week, and day five hundred eighty-one.

chat.says: What is sakinah? I keep hearing the word.
options: A stillness Allah sends down into troubled hearts, as at Hudaybiyyah.
A calm you reach on your own by controlling your breathing well.
The silence kept in a mosque during the Friday sermon.
chat.meaning: 48:4 says He sent down sakinah into the believers' hearts. The verse doesn't say they calmed themselves; calm was given, and added faith to faith.
